implemented_requirements.evidence: config.py defines GRID_SIZE = 4; Game.__init__ creates a size‑GRID_SIZE board; renderer draws GRID_SIZE rows and columns.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Tile movement via arrow keys (or WASD)
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py maps pygame.K_LEFT / K_a to game.move('left'), K_RIGHT / K_d to 'right', K_UP / K_w to 'up', K_DOWN / K_s to 'down'.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Merging equal tiles and doubling value
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game._slide_row_left merges adjacent equal values, creates merged = tiles[i] * 2, adds to score.
Game.move adds gained points to self.score; Renderer._draw_header displays game.score.
Game.highest_tile returns max tile; Renderer._draw_header shows it as 'BEST TILE'.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Spawn a new tile (2 or 4) after each successful move
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.move calls self.spawn_tile() when moved is True; spawn_tile places a 2 (90%) or 4 (10%) in a random empty cell.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends when no moves are possible
implemented_requirements.evidence: After a move, Game.can_move() is checked; if False, self.game_over is set. Renderer draws overlay when game.game_over is True.
Game._check_win sets self.won when TARGET_TILE (2048) is on the board; Renderer shows a win banner.

judge.summary: All core features of a standard 2048 game are present: a 4x4 board, arrow/WASD controls, merging logic, score and highest tile display, random tile spawning, win detection, and game‑over handling. The code is syntactically correct and should run with pygame installed, giving a high likelihood of successful execution.
